name: Salak Geothermal Well #1
location: East Awibengkok Sector, Gunung Salak Field, West Java
rockTypeNote: Field-level characterization from regional geology literature; not well-specific core/log data for Well #1
rockTypeSource: Stimac et al. (2008), as cited across multiple Salak field geology papers
anomalyDescription: Decline rate escalated from an 8% baseline to 23% (production interference, early 2005) then 237% (silica scale blockage, late 2006). Confirmed via sinker bar survey; recovered scale sample was 80% amorphous silica at 3730 ft-md. Resolved via mechanical workover, June 2007.

productionHistory.unitNote: Steam rate in kilo-pounds per hour (kph); decline rate in percent per year

points.eventDescription: Well #1 completed at TD 5120 ft-md in the East Awibengkok steam cap reservoir. Initial production 280 kph at a normal decline rate of 8%. This is the well's baseline.

Decline rate rose to 23%. A new production well was drilled into the same reservoir sector and a neighboring well converted from two-phase to dry steam, increasing total field extraction from the East Salak steam cap.
Steam rate still at 190 kph, the level immediately before the sharp drop described below.

Steam rate dropped from 190 to 90 kph with no change in neighboring wells' extraction rate. Sinker bar survey (2.25" tool) found a blockage at 3730 ft-md; recovered scale sample was 80% amorphous silica by petrographic analysis.

Mechanical clean-out of scale performed. Production recovered to a level consistent with the well's hydraulic model, confirming the decline was caused exclusively by wellbore scale, not formation-level damage.

name: Silangkitang Northernmost Production Well
coordinateNote: Approximate — derived from field's reported distance (~35 km SE of Tarutung); exact well coordinates not published
location: Silangkitang (SIL) Field, Tapanuli Utara, North Sumatra
rockType: Metasediments (marble, phyllite, argillite, meta-quartzite) basement, overlain by Tertiary conglomerate/greywacke/mudstone
rockTypeNote: Field-level characterization; not well-specific core/log data
anomalyDescription: Chemical breakthrough detected: NCG and HCO3 declining since injection began (2017), consistent with injectate liquid (low-NCG, low-HCO3) reaching this well from SIL 2 injection pad. Confirmed by tracer test showing 1.59% cumulative mass return from SIL 2 injectors within 4 months. However, no thermal breakthrough detected — enthalpy remains stable and flow rate has increased, attributed to reservoir boiling and sufficient residence time for injectate to reheat before reaching the well.

geochemicalHistory.unitNote: NCG in weight %, HCO3 in ppm, enthalpy in kJ/kg, flow rate in tonnes/hour
geochemicalHistory.dataQuality: Digitized approximate values from Figure 11(b), Simatupang et al. (2020) — not exact text-quoted figures

points.eventDescription: Early monitoring point shortly after commercial production began (Mar 2017 for full field; this well among initial producers). NCG and HCO3 at reservoir-characteristic levels.
NCG and HCO3 trending downward, consistent with early injectate liquid arrival from SIL 2 injection wells to the north.
NCG and HCO3 continuing to decline. Enthalpy remains stable, indicating no thermal impact despite chemical dilution.

points.eventLabel: Confirmed chemical breakthrough, no thermal impact
points.eventDescription: NCG and HCO3 at lowest observed levels (~30% decline from baseline). Enthalpy and flow rate both stable-to-increasing, confirming injectate liquid has been sufficiently reheated by reservoir rock (>280°C) before reaching this well.

source: Simatupang, C., Matsuda, K. and Astra, D. (2020). The Initial State Geochemical Model and Reservoir Response of 2 Years Production at Silangkitang, a Fault-Controlled Geothermal System along the Great Sumatera Fault. Proceedings World Geothermal Congress 2020, Reykjavik.
